headline: Pittsfield rail work could turn Berkshire Flyer into a permanent seasonal link
dek: A new MassDOT-CSX agreement calls for track improvements near Pittsfield, aimed at reducing freight conflicts and creating a more durable passenger rail connection to New York City.
body: A new agreement between the Massachusetts Department of Transportation and CSX could move the Berkshire Flyer from a recurring summer experiment toward permanent seasonal weekend service, while also laying groundwork for a broader passenger-rail network in Western Massachusetts. The [MassDOT announcement](https://www.mass.gov/news/governor-healey-announces-major-step-toward-permanent-berkshire-flyer-service-expanded-passenger-rail-in-western-massachusetts) says the state will fund a siding and other track improvements in the Pittsfield area under the agreement with the freight railroad.

The work is intended to increase capacity on a corridor where passenger and freight trains compete for room. MassDOT also plans to study whether a new platform could be built at Pittsfield Station. The department included $31 million for the Pittsfield track-capacity project in its fiscal 2027-2031 capital plan. That money is a state funding commitment for planned infrastructure; it is not a promise that the siding, platform or permanent service will be operating immediately.

The operating problem is specific to the railroad’s layout. [GBH News reported](https://www.wgbh.org/news/local/2026-10-08/state-csx-agree-to-rail-upgrades-in-the-berkshires) that long stretches of the CSX-owned route between Albany and Pittsfield are single track, and that MassDOT has said freight conflicts have hurt the Berkshire Flyer’s on-time performance. A siding would give trains a place to pass or wait, potentially reducing conflicts, although the state has not published a final construction schedule or a new passenger timetable.

The Berkshire Flyer currently links Pittsfield with New York City on a seasonal, weekend schedule operated by Amtrak with MassDOT support. The service began in 2022, and the 2026 season added another round trip. [Amtrak’s 2026 service announcement](https://media.amtrak.com/2026/05/amtraks-berkshire-flyer-returns-for-summer-service-with-expanded-weekend-trips-between-pittsfield-and-new-york-city/) described trains running from Moynihan Train Hall through Albany-Rensselaer and other Hudson Valley stops to the Joseph Scelsi Intermodal Transportation Center in Pittsfield. The 2026 schedule ran from June 12 through Sept. 13, so the new agreement concerns future seasons rather than an immediate year-round train.

For Pittsfield and Berkshire County, the value of the connection is measured in more than visitor counts. The route gives residents an alternative to driving for trips to New York and gives visitors a direct rail option for the region’s cultural, recreational and business destinations. Pittsfield Mayor Peter Marchetti called the connection an important city asset in the state’s release, while officials have presented better rail access as a way to support local businesses and strengthen the region’s ties to the wider Northeast Corridor.

The Pittsfield work is also part of a larger Massachusetts plan called Compass Rail. The state is pursuing an Inland Route between Boston, Springfield and New Haven and studying additional service along the Boston-Albany corridor. The [GBH report](https://www.wgbh.org/news/local/2026-10-08/state-csx-agree-to-rail-upgrades-in-the-berkshires) described the Berkshire Flyer, the proposed East-West rail service and other intercity routes as pieces of that broader vision. Those projects have different funding, design and approval paths, so progress on one does not establish a launch date for the others.

The announcement also points to newer equipment as part of the long-term plan. MassDOT said Amtrak received about $2 billion in federal funding through the Federal Railroad Administration’s National Railroad Partnership Program for additional Siemens Airo trainsets, which are expected to support services including the Berkshire Flyer and the planned Inland Route. The trains and the Pittsfield track work address different constraints: newer equipment can improve the passenger experience, while the siding and related changes are meant to give trains more operating capacity.

The next meaningful milestones will be design and construction decisions, followed by a confirmed seasonal schedule. Until those steps are complete, travelers should treat permanent Berkshire Flyer service as an objective supported by a new infrastructure agreement, not as a service already guaranteed. The immediate development is the state’s commitment to improve the Pittsfield-area railroad so passenger trains can operate with fewer conflicts on a line that also remains important to CSX’s freight network.
author: NorthEast News Desk
seoTitle: Pittsfield rail work could make Berkshire Flyer permanent
seoDescription: MassDOT and CSX agreed to Pittsfield-area track improvements aimed at reducing freight conflicts and supporting permanent seasonal Berkshire Flyer service.
